result.title: You Only Think Once: Rescuing Hybrid Vision-Language Models Lost in Thought
result.summary: Thinking at length before answering is expected to strengthen the visual reasoning of vision-language models (VLMs), yet hybrid VLMs often get lost in thought: their thoughts loop or exhaust the budget without an answer, so thinking can score below answering directly. Existing early-exit methods watch a thought for the moment its answer is ready and force the answer out of it, but in a hybrid VLM that moment often never comes. We find that the remedy is not to stop a failing thought earlier, but to stop taking its answer: once a thought is given up, the model's own direct answers decide. Based on this, we propose **YOTO (You Only Think Once)**, a method that answers first and thinks at most once. YOTO draws direct answers until a probe-weighted vote settles; only an unsettled problem receives a single thought, which a failure head on the hidden state monitors and stops as soon as it predicts failure, handing the problem back to direct answers. At a matched 20k-token budget, YOTO is up to 5.9 points more accurate than the strongest early-exit baseline, using one failure-head threshold across model sizes. Keeping the released weights frozen, it adds only two linear probes. On the full MathVision benchmark, YOTO improves Qwen3.5-2B from 40.1% to 57.3% and Qwen3.5-4B from 68.3% to 73.7%, above the 72.8% that Qwen3.5-9B, a model more than twice its size, reaches with thinking. Its gains carry over to five further benchmarks and a second model family. These results suggest that hybrid VLMs reason better by answering first and thinking once than by thinking longer.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 YOTO：先多次直接作答并用探针加权投票判断是否收敛，仅对未收敛问题进行一次思考，再由隐状态上的失败头预测失败并提前终止、回退到直接答案。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及 VLM 中 THINK/STOP 的收益与成本，把停止决策落实为隐状态失败预测和回答回退机制；可供核查失败头依赖推理内容还是表层信号，以及单一阈值在不同模型规模与长度上的泛化。
